codeInspection: Embedded visibilityParts remains the shared polyhedral/sphere core; body faces alone occlude auxiliary construction strokes.
Camera direction is the inverse rotated positive depth axis. Polyhedral faces including concave cut-box polygons use full interval splitting; visible and hidden layers preserve stroke registration.

roundVisibilityParts derives the correct cylinder/cone quadratic along the viewing ray. Parameter cuts cover physical side intersections, ray tangencies, height crossings, and ray intersections with top/bottom rim circles; tube inner-wall radii are included.
Ray/quadric tangencies do not invent positive-length occlusion. Enabled caps and component ownership preserve the hollow tube and the cylinder-cone internal join.
The duplicated cylinder-cone seam was removed from the cylinder upper-rim stroke; the cone bottom seam is rendered once. The independently found front-seam misclassification is resolved.
Explicit curved-surface arcs and actual generators use smooth-normal ownership; interior chords/radii do not receive this exemption. Analytic spheres classify radii and diameters behind the surface.

Curve dash phase uses cumulative projected chord arclength. Canonical endpoint/adjacent-point comparison reverses consistently; split intervals continue the phase from their original start. Straight coincident strokes retain global canonical phase.

Top-cap front visibility relies on the existing validated positive pitch range [0.14, 1.25]. Below-body views are not currently permitted; changing that range would require a sign-aware top-cap condition.
